positive.point: Acuity Scheduling is recommended for its integration with Microsoft 365, custom intake questions, and ease of embedding into websites.
Subscription calendars for businesses with rotating schedules have been effective in keeping customers informed without relying on social media algorithms.
Notion and Slack integration via make.com can automate data transfer and is cost-effective for small teams.
Dedicated mini-apps for specific tasks, like site inspections, are preferred over general-purpose databases like Airtable for ease of use in the field.
Styloving aims to provide a comprehensive salon management system at an accessible price for small businesses.
Toggl and Clockify are recommended for solo business owners to track time across various tasks effectively.

negative.point: Microsoft Bookings and Calendly have been found to be buggy and unreliable, with issues like emails going to spam.
Social media posts for schedule updates are unreliable due to algorithm limitations and short visibility.
Airtable can become cluttered and is not ideal for non-technical field users who need a simple interface.
Managing communication and important information across multiple channels is challenging for growing businesses.
Existing tools for managing field operations are often outdated, expensive, or not tailored for field work.
